annotations.text:
WAVE 3 - CLOSING PHASE 0
Issue #325 - Epic #323

Waves 1 and 2 ran four imagery tracks as rivals. The rubric decision later
that same day ended that contest: never bare type, personal > sourced >
derived, Track A demoted to a text layer, B and C collapsed into one tier-3
floor. Wave 3 does not re-run the vote. It tests the SYSTEM the rubric
implies, and answers the exit criteria still open.

THE LAYOUT: A FULL-BLEED MEDIA BAND, TYPE ENTIRELY BELOW IT.
The image runs edge to edge and takes 820 of the card's 1350 - 61%, and 46%
more area than the inset square an earlier cut of this wave used.

Why type stays outside. This is the part of the square-well idea that was
actually load-bearing: nothing sits on the photograph, so there is no scrim,
no legibility risk, and no long artist name fighting a busy frame. Compare
Main against 'The counter-case' at the end of this row - same photograph,
type laid over it.

Why one band height for every tier. An earlier cut scaled the well by tier,
on the theory that the layout should answer to the strength of the asset. The
nine-up grid killed it: the small-well tiles read as broken, a stranded square
over an empty field, not as hierarchy. Tier now decides WHICH image is
fetched and nothing else. What carries the grid instead is the GROUND - dark
against paper - which is the only variation still legible at 124px.

WHAT EACH TIER COSTS AT THIS SIZE, measured rather than asserted:
  Tier 1, personal      - 3000px+ originals. Free.
  Tier 2, album cover   - Cover Art Archive serves front-1200. Free, once the
                          pipeline stops asking for front-500.
  Tier 2, artist shot   - 700x700 is the ceiling. 1.54x upscale, 19% cropped.
                          The only real cost in the system.
  Tier 3, derived       - authored AT the frame, so no scaling at all.

NAMES ARE STRUCTURAL FURNITURE, not something a generated hook is trusted to
contain. Artist, song, venue and date come off the record, each on its own
line, so they cannot be omitted by accident. This reversed a Wave 2 decision:
the withheld-name cards were unfindable by search, gave a scrolling fan no
reason to stop, and on Instagram - where captions carry no clickable link -
teased a reveal the reader had no way to reach. Withhold the interpretation;
never the identification.

THE MARK. "MORPERHAUS" in the corner was dead weight: invisible at feed scale,
and on Bluesky the handle IS concerts.morperhaus.org, so it said nothing twice.
It is now the URL itself, broken across three staggered lines with the brand
pulled left as the anchor - a mark rather than a caption. It survives on the
4:5 card, where the image travels without any surrounding context; the 1.91:1
link card already sits under the handle and does not need it.

PROVENANCE IS ONE FIELD WITH TWO STATES, and it is what finally separates
tier 1 from tier 2. "My photograph · 31 July 2026" on a personal frame;
"My photograph · 2026, not the 1987 night" when the shot is from another
night, which the voice rules require. Tier 2 and tier 3 carry no chip at all -
so the mark is earned, and a personal frame visibly outranks a press shot
instead of being indistinguishable from one.

It rides IN the image, bottom-left, because a card gets screenshotted without
its caption and a claim about whose photograph this is has to travel with the
picture.

TIER 1 - PERSONAL - FULL WELL

The top of the rubric, and now a real photograph: Mike's own frame of Nile
Rodgers at the Pacific Amphitheatre - the actual second night this post is
about.

THE CROP IS THE ARGUMENT. A centre-square crop of the landscape original
keeps Rodgers, the white Strat and the horn player.

HEADS UP: this is the tighter frame that was already living in the canvas -
1080x700, stage only. The wider version you pasted into the session, with the
band of raised phones across the crowd, never reached disk and is the better
file: the phones are what say a person was standing there, and no generated
treatment can fake them. Drop that one in as nile-rodgers-2026.jpg and this
board gets stronger for free.

Nothing sits on the photograph. The hook has the lower quarter of the card to
itself, so there is no scrim and no legibility risk. Compare against 'The
counter-case' at the end of this row, which is the same photograph with the
type laid over it.

The chip bottom-left is the provenance field - see the brief. It is the only
thing distinguishing this card from the tier-2 one beside it, which is the
point: personal imagery should visibly outrank sourced.

Watch for: whether 72px reads at feed scale once the band takes the top 61%
of the card. If it does not, the hook budget shrinks - and that is a payload
field, not a design note.

TIER 2 - SOURCED, ARTIST - THE ONE REAL COST

The workhorse, and the mocks had never drawn it: 46 of the 57 published notes
resolve here, to a 700x700 fan-uploaded press shot on one host. Exactly ONE
resolves to Cover Art Archive.

700px is a hard ceiling, so this is the only tier where a bigger image is not
free: filling the 1080-wide band means 1.54x and crops 19% off the square's
height. At feed scale, roughly 400px delivered, that is invisible. At 100%
zoom it is soft. Judge it here at full size and decide whether the softness
costs more than one consistent layout does.

The album path has no such problem - see the tier-2 album board. Cover Art
Archive serves front-1200 and the pipeline currently asks for front-500.

Watch for: this card is now identical to tier 1 apart from the image itself,
so a viewer cannot tell a personal photograph from a press shot. Given
'personal beats sourced' is the rubric's core, that may want a mark.

TIER 2 - SOURCED, ALBUM - FULL WELL, PAPER GROUND

When the post's subject IS the record, the cover earns the full well: square
by nature, defensible, and about the thing being discussed.

Paper ground on purpose. A feed of nothing but ink cards recedes. Giving the
album treatment the light ground means roughly one card in five is bright,
and the rhythm comes from the routing rather than from a decision.

Real post: Social Distortion at The Belasco, December 2024 - four songs from
Born to Kill 519 days before the record existed.

Watch for: whether light and dark cards still read as one account.

TIER 3 - DERIVED - AUTHORED AT THE FRAME

The floor, not the default - and the tier that had been quietly wasting the
most. The previous cut drew this in a 936x936 viewBox and rendered it at 780,
discarding 17% of the linework for nothing. Derived artwork has no source
file and therefore no ceiling: it is generated to whatever frame we ask for,
so it should be authored AT the frame. The viewBox is now 1080x820, 1:1.

Same for the material treatment on the Stress page: a designed stub has no
resolution ceiling either.

Bars are real per-year show counts, 1984-2026.

Watch for: this treatment needs a story with a SHAPE - a span, a gap, a
repeat. A one-off show has nothing to draw, which is what 'The true floor'
on the Stress page answers.

THE COUNTER-CASE - FULL BLEED, TYPE OVER IMAGE

The same photograph as Main, treated Wave 2's way, drawn fairly rather than
strawmanned so the tradeoff is visible instead of asserted.

WHAT IT COSTS, and both costs are on screen:
1. Filling 1080x1350 from a landscape frame needs a 1.93x upscale and throws
   away 48 per cent of the width. Both crowd edges are gone.
2. To make 90px type legible over a lit stage you need a scrim across the
   bottom 55 per cent - and that scrim covers the phones, which were the
   whole reason the photograph was worth having.

WHAT IT BUYS: the image is bigger and more immediate, and it is the more
conventional social format. That is a real argument.

Decide this by looking, not by reasoning. And note that picking full bleed
makes the tier-2 supply problem worse, not better: those sources are 700px
square, so full bleed upscales every one of them 1.54x.

THE NINE-UP GRID - THE ROBOTIC TEST

The spec's own acceptance criterion, and the test no wave has run. Both grids
hold the SAME nine real published posts, drawn from the first dozen and
chosen to include the worst of the template repetition rather than to be a
literal consecutive run.

THE FINDING, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN LAYOUT: 28 of the 57 published headlines
follow one of five detector templates. 'Caught Once, Never Again' alone
accounts for 9. Grid A shows three of them adjacent, verbatim.

So the account reads as a bot because of the COPY, not the cards. No amount
of art direction fixes Grid A. This is the number behind the spec's
'authored, never derived' rule - it was a principle, and now it is measured.

Grid B changes two things: the hook is written per post, and the ARTIST IS
NAMED on every card. At 124px the name is the only legible text on a tile -
the hook is noise at that size - which is the clearest argument for naming. Judge the 124px strip at the bottom, not the large tiles - that
is a phone profile grid at true scale.

Also worth noting: five of these nine shows are at the Pacific Amphitheatre.
Venue repetition is a second, smaller version of the same problem.

THE SCROLL - BLUESKY AT 600px, TRUE FEED SCALE

Neighbouring posts are skeletons on purpose. The question is whether ours
holds a scroll, and inventing other people's posts to answer it would be
fabrication.

Note what the link card is NOT: it is 1.91:1, not the 4:5 card. Bluesky,
Mastodon and X all take the wide card; only Instagram takes 4:5. That is two
render targets from day one, which the media ladder already calls L0.

The thumbnail has to be uploaded as a blob - Bluesky will not scrape our OG
tag - and the facets need BYTE offsets, not character offsets.

Watch for: the hook reads at 15px here. It is the same sentence that is 72px
on the Instagram card. If one length cannot serve both, the payload needs a
per-channel budget rather than one hook.

THE CAROUSEL - THE SCHEMA DECIDER

This is the artboard that settles hook vs beats, which is the one Phase 0
output that breaks every adapter if it is guessed wrong.

Counts under each pane are LIVE - computed from the strings above them, not
typed in. The longest beat is the budget - 109 characters, on beat 3.

Pane 1 carries imagery, per the rule. Panes 2-5 are text-only, which the rule
permits. The loop closes on pane 4 rather than being held for the permalink,
because Instagram captions have no clickable link: the carousel's job there
is dwell and saves, not clicks.

If this arc holds, the payload is hook: string AND beats: string[] - hook
always, beats optional and consumed only by carousel-capable adapters.

Watch for: whether beat 3 is doing too much work at 109 characters. If it
needs splitting, the answer is 6 panes, not a longer budget.

ON THIS DAY - DATE-FORWARD ARCHITECTURE

The exit criterion says date-forward, not headline-forward, and these three
take it literally: a masthead with the date and a rule under it. That is the
signature that separates the two streams at a glance in a feed - a liner note
leads with a sentence, an On This Day leads with a date.

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: a multi-show date has no single subject, so no tier-1
or tier-2 image can be routed to it. Busy dates fall to tier 3 BY
CONSTRUCTION. On the four-show card the year spine IS the tier-3 artwork
rather than decoration laid over it. Only three dates in the archive carry
four shows.

The anniversary card gets the paper ground: 25 round anniversaries land in
2026, they score highest, and the best post of the year should not look like
the other 144.

Watch for: whether the masthead is enough separation, or whether the two
streams need different palettes.

THE WORST-CASE CORPUS

Every record here is real and comes from corpus.json.

LONGEST ARTIST NAME - 'Richard Cheese & Lounge Against the Machine' (43ch)
opening for 'The Brian Setzer Orchestra' (26ch), Universal Amphitheater,
21 Dec 2002. 69 characters of proper noun in one hook. The square well is
what saves it: the hook owns the lower half, so it wraps instead of
overflowing.

LONGEST VENUE NAME - 'National Museum of African American History and
Culture' (55ch), longer than any artist name and in the position with the
least room. The Roots played it 24 Sep 2016. Both footers on that board are
the same string: the red one carries the white-space:nowrap that every Wave 2
board used and overflows; the green one wraps. Wave 2 shipped the red one.

THE TRUE FLOOR - no image resolves AND the post has no span, gap or repeat,
so derived has nothing to draw either. The answer is the material stub: it
needs only a date, an artist and a venue, which every record in the archive
has by definition. That is what makes 'never bare type' a rule we can
actually keep. Wave 2's Track C survives here - as the fallback, not as the
house style.

CROSS-CHANNEL SHEET, AND THE DISCLOSURE

Whether four channels read as one brand is invisible until they are adjacent.

TEXT BUDGET, SETTLED: the authored hook plus its turn is 109 characters. That
clears X at 280 and Bluesky at 300 with room to spare, so the tightest
channel does NOT force a shorter hook. The counters on each column are
computed from the string, not typed.

THE DIFFERENT-NIGHT DISCLOSURE - a recommendation, not a decision. It is
drawn in-image here, in the well's bottom-left. The argument: a card gets
screenshotted and re-shared without its caption, and a claim about which
night a photograph is from has to travel with the picture. In-caption is
cheaper and reads better; it also silently disappears the moment anyone
screenshots the card.

X gets its link in the first self-reply, built in from the start. Instagram
gets no clickable link at all, which is why its adapter is the one that
consumes beats[].

THE IDENTITY

The spec calls profile copy a Phase 0 output rather than an afterthought, and
it is the surface every visitor sees before a single post.

The avatar has to survive 32px, so it is one letterform on the ink ground -
shown at 168, 56 and 32 so the smallest size is judged rather than assumed.
A wordmark would be mud at 32px.

Bio copy is the archive's own voice and its own numbers, and it ends on a
cadence promise rather than a tagline. 'One person who kept the stubs' is
the line doing the work - it says this is not a brand account.

The bio link goes to /liner-notes, never the homepage: newest-first means the
top post is always the one the caption just referred to.

Open question for you: the handle. Bluesky can be concerts.morperhaus.org via
DNS TXT, which is free and self-verifying. The other platforms cannot, so
they need a name - and it should be registered everywhere at once, including
the out-of-scope platforms, before someone else takes it.

WAVES 1 AND 2 - KEPT AS THE RECORD

These are the four-track contest, preserved unchanged. They are not live
candidates: the imagery rubric decided later the same day that Track A is a
text layer rather than a card, and that B and C are one tier-3 floor.

What survives from them and carried into Wave 3:
- The open loop. Withholding who played it the second time is the best single
  move in Wave 2 and it is in every Wave 3 hook.
- Big type. Wave 1's 18-21px footers were invisible at feed scale.
- Track C's stub, promoted from a house style to the tier-3 floor.
- Track D landing on a real photograph, which the rubric then codified.

What did NOT survive: the shared bottom furniture. All four Wave 2 cards end
with the same rule, the same prompt, the same venue line and the same
wordmark in the same order at the same sizes - four aesthetics wearing one
uniform. And 'Were you at either one?' cannot be a slot a generator fills
weekly; it is a real question from someone who was there exactly once. It is
absent from every Wave 3 card so the grids can be judged without it.

CAPTION COPY - AND THE TAG QUESTION

You asked what text should travel with the media, and whether it carries
hashtags. The answer is not one answer: tags do opposite things on the four
channels, so a single house rule would be wrong on three of them.

MASTODON needs them most. No recommendation algorithm at all, and full-text
search is opt-in per user - so hashtags are close to the only way a post is
discovered. 4-5, and CamelCase (#NileRodgers, not #nilerodgers), which is a
firm accessibility norm there: screen readers can parse the word boundaries.

X gets NONE. The platform has discouraged them, and they eat the tightest
budget we have. The link is not in the post either - it goes in the first
self-reply.

BLUESKY takes 1-2, inline. They are real (clickable facets, followable feeds)
but stacking reads as spam. They ride as facets on byte offsets, which is the
same machinery the link already needs, so they cost nothing extra to build.

INSTAGRAM takes 3-5, in the caption. The 30-tag block is obsolete and keyword
search now carries a lot of discovery. Put them in the caption: the
'hashtags in the first comment' trick is folklore.

WHERE TAGS COME FROM: entities the record already knows - artist, venue,
city, decade. Generated, not authored, and they are what a stranger would
actually type.

WHAT MUST NEVER SHIP: the detector tags. liner-notes.json carries
#full-circle and #cover on this very post. That is internal taxonomy - it
means nothing to a reader and it is an instant tell that a machine wrote the
post. The adapter has to suppress them.

Note the structure: ONE core sentence pair, authored once, reused verbatim on
all four. Only the link and the tags differ. That is the 'one payload, N dumb
adapters' rule made visible - and it is why the counts stay comfortable even
on X.

THE WIDE CARD - 1200x630

Bluesky, Mastodon and X all render this format. Three of four channels, and
until now it existed only as a 275px thumbnail on the timeline board. Every
other post artboard in this canvas is the Instagram 4:5.

A - STACKED. The 4:5 system scaled down. The band cannot hold 61% here; at
340 (54%) the type fits, but the hook drops 72px -> 44px and the meta loses a
line.

That much was arithmetic. What only the render shows is the disqualifying
part: 1200x340 is a 3.5:1 letterbox, and it BEHEADS THE SUBJECT. Rodgers'
face is above the crop. Now apply that to tier 2 - every sourced image we
have is square, so a 700x700 press shot becomes a 2:1 band across someone's
eyes. This option structurally cannot hold the imagery the archive has.

B - SQUARE PLUS COLUMN. 630x630 image, 570 type column.

The 1.91:1 frame turns out to be the one place a square image is the natural
fit rather than a compromise. A 700x700 press shot renders at 630 - the only
format in the whole system where tier 2 is DOWNSCALED. No upscale, no crop,
no decapitation. The hook keeps a real column and holds 50px.

RECOMMENDATION: B, and not on taste - A fails on the actual image supply.

The cost of B, stated plainly: it is a second composition, sharing only its
parts with the 4:5 card. Two render targets, two layouts. That is the price
of the wide format existing at all, and it is cheaper than the alternative,
which is publishing beheaded press shots to three of four channels.

Watch for: the hook is the same string in both formats and it holds. If a
longer hook ever needs a second, shorter budget, THIS is the format that
forces it - which would be a payload change, not a layout tweak.
